config.title: useOnlineStatus

intro.title: useOnlineStatus
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useOnlineStatus` that tracks whether the user's browser is currently online or offline. You will learn how to use the browser's `navigator.onLine` property and the `online`/`offline` window events to monitor network connectivity in real-time. The main technologies involved are React hooks, specifically `useState` for state management and `useEffect` for handling side effects like event listeners. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that returns a boolean value, allowing any component to easily respond to changes in network status.
intro.usecase: The useOnlineStatus hook is essential for building resilient applications that handle network connectivity changes gracefully. In real-world products like Google Docs or Figma, you'll see status indicators that show 'Offline' or 'Syncing' when internet connection drops, preventing data loss. E-commerce checkout flows use this pattern to disable payment buttons and show warnings when users lose connectivity mid-transaction. Streaming platforms like Netflix or YouTube implement similar logic to pause playback and display reconnection messages when network issues occur. Developers use this hook to create better user experiences by adapting UI behavior based on real-time network availability.

objectives: Apply the useState hook to create and manage a boolean state variable for online status
Use the useEffect hook to set up event listeners for online/offline events
Implement event handler functions to update state when network status changes
Execute conditional cleanup logic to remove event listeners when the component unmounts
Construct a custom hook function with proper TypeScript return type annotations
Utilize the window.navigator.onLine property to initialize the online status state
Assign appropriate event types ('online' and 'offline') to addEventListener and removeEventListener calls
Control component side effects by specifying an empty dependency array in useEffect
Return the current online status value from the custom hook for consumption by components
Define a reusable custom hook that encapsulates the network status monitoring logic
Invoke the custom useOnlineStatus hook within React components to access real-time network status
Modify component rendering behavior based on the boolean value returned by useOnlineStatus

steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package. This will allow you to use React components and state management in your TypeScript project.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';

steps.expectedOutcome: You should see the import statement at the top of your file, making React and useState available for use.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and state management capabilities.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Make sure the syntax is correct.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Remember to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the useOnlineStatus custom hook
steps.instruction: Create a custom hook function called 'useOnlineStatus' that returns a boolean value. Place it after the imports and before your component.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns a boolean. You can start with a placeholder return value like 'true' or 'false' for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'useOnlineStatus' that returns a boolean type.
successCriteria: The code should contain a function declaration or arrow function named 'useOnlineStatus' that returns a boolean value (e.g., true or false). The function should be placed after the imports.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the useOnlineStatus custom hook. This is the foundation we'll build upon to add actual online/offline detection logic.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named exactly 'useOnlineStatus' and returns a boolean value (true or false).
steps.feedbackWrong: The custom hook wasn't created correctly. Please create a function called 'useOnlineStatus' that returns a boolean value.

steps.title: Initialize online status state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside your useOnlineStatus custom hook, call useState to create a state variable named 'isOnline' and initialize it with the current browser online status from 'navigator.onLine'.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The initial state should be the boolean value from navigator.onLine.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your useOnlineStatus hook will have a state variable 'isOnline' initialized to the browser's current online status.
successCriteria: The code should include a useState call inside useOnlineStatus that creates a state variable named 'isOnline' initialized with 'navigator.onLine'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the online status state using useState. The 'isOnline' variable will now track whether the browser is online or offline.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've: 1) Called useState inside the useOnlineStatus hook, 2) Named the state variable 'isOnline', and 3) Initialized it with 'navigator.onLine'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the useOnlineStatus function, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'isOnline' and set its initial value to 'navigator.onLine'.

steps.title: Define the updateOnlineStatus handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your useOnlineStatus hook, create a function named updateOnlineStatus that sets the isOnline state to navigator.onLine.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setIsOnline with navigator.onLine as the argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your useOnlineStatus hook will have a function that can update the isOnline state based on the browser's online status.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the updateOnlineStatus handler function that will update the online status state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named exactly 'updateOnlineStatus' and calls setIsOnline with navigator.onLine.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to create a function called updateOnlineStatus that sets isOnline to navigator.onLine.

steps.title: Add event listeners for online/offline events
steps.instruction: Inside your useOnlineStatus hook, add event listeners for the 'online' and 'offline' events on the window object. Both listeners should call the updateOnlineStatus function you defined earlier.
steps.hint: Use window.addEventListener('online', updateOnlineStatus) and window.addEventListener('offline', updateOnlineStatus) to listen for network status changes.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your useOnlineStatus hook will now listen for network connectivity changes and update the isOnline state accordingly.
successCriteria: The code should include two window.addEventListener calls: one for 'online' and one for 'offline', both calling updateOnlineStatus.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added event listeners to track network status changes. The hook will now update automatically when the user goes online or offline.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both event listeners: one for 'online' and one for 'offline'. Both should call the updateOnlineStatus function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The event listeners for network status changes are missing. Remember to use window.addEventListener for both 'online' and 'offline' events, calling updateOnlineStatus for each.

steps.title: Return cleanup function for event listeners
steps.instruction: Inside your useOnlineStatus hook, return a cleanup function that removes the 'online' and 'offline' event listeners from the window object. This function should be returned from the hook so React can call it when the component unmounts.
steps.hint: Return an arrow function that calls window.removeEventListener for both 'online' and 'offline' events, using the same updateOnlineStatus handler you'll add in the next step.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useOnlineStatus hook now returns a cleanup function that will properly remove event listeners when the component using this hook unmounts.
successCriteria: The hook should return an arrow function that calls window.removeEventListener for both 'online' and 'offline' events with the updateOnlineStatus handler.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've added the cleanup function that will remove the event listeners when the component unmounts. This prevents memory leaks and ensures proper cleanup.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the cleanup function needs to remove both event listeners. Make sure you're calling window.removeEventListener for both 'online' and 'offline' events with the updateOnlineStatus handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanup function should remove both event listeners. Try returning an arrow function that calls window.removeEventListener for 'online' and 'offline' events with the updateOnlineStatus handler.

steps.title: Return the isOnline state from the hook
steps.instruction: Return the `isOnline` state variable from the `useOnlineStatus` hook so components can use it.
steps.hint: At the end of your hook function, add a return statement that returns the `isOnline` variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The hook now returns the current online status value, making it available to any component that calls `useOnlineStatus()`.
successCriteria: The hook returns the `isOnline` state variable
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned the online status from your custom hook. Now components can call `useOnlineStatus()` and get the current online status value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning the `isOnline` variable from the hook function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook needs to return the `isOnline` state variable so components can access the current online status.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a function component called App that returns a div element.
steps.hint: Define a component named App using either a function declaration or arrow function. Make sure it returns a JSX element (like a div).
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named App is created, returning a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component. This will serve as the main component that uses our custom hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but something is missing. Make sure you define a component named App and that it returns a JSX element (like a div).
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't properly defined. You need to create a function component called App that returns a div element.

steps.title: Use the useOnlineStatus hook in App component
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, call the useOnlineStatus hook and store its return value in a variable.
steps.hint: Call the hook like you would call useState or any other hook, and assign the result to a variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now has access to the online status state returned by the custom hook.
successCriteria: The code should call useOnlineStatus() inside the App component and assign its return value to a variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully called the useOnlineStatus hook in your App component. This gives you access to the current online status state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling the useOnlineStatus hook inside the App component and storing its return value in a variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component should call the useOnlineStatus hook and store its return value. Look at the analogous example for how to call a custom hook.

steps.title: Display the online status in the UI
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, return JSX that displays 'Online' when isOnline is true and 'Offline' when isOnline is false.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to conditionally render different text based on the isOnline value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component returns JSX that conditionally displays 'Online' or 'Offline' text based on the online status state.
successCriteria: Uses ternary operator for conditional rendering
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented conditional rendering to display the online status in the UI. The App component now shows 'Online' when connected and 'Offline' when disconnected.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the isOnline value from the hook and conditionally rendering the correct text. Check that you're using a ternary operator like: {isOnline ? 'Online' : 'Offline'}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component doesn't yet display the online status. Remember to return JSX that shows 'Online' when isOnline is true and 'Offline' when isOnline is false, using the isOnline value from the hook.
